history.idea: Replace the random-order baseline with a target-similarity filter plus junk/duplicate removal. Steps: (1) Fit a char n-gram (1-3, analyzer='char', lowercase=False) HashingVectorizer/TF-IDF on the first ~2000 chars of each doc; train a LogisticRegression with positives = target_sample (chunked into several 2000-char pieces to get more positives) and negatives = a seeded random sample of ~3000 pool docs (PU-learning style); score every pool doc by predicted probability of being target-domain (WikiText-style: '= Title =' headers, ' @-@ ', ' , ' spaced punctuation). (2) Drop exact duplicates (hash of whitespace-normalised text) and near-duplicates (same first 200 chars), keeping one copy. (3) Drop damaged docs: boilerplate with heavy line repetition (unique-line ratio < 0.5 or zlib compression ratio < 0.2), and word-shuffled docs detected by a target-trained word-bigram check: build the set of word bigrams from target_sample, and for each doc compute the fraction of its bigrams among the first 300 words that appear in that set; shuffled docs (e.g. 'bridge U.S. @-@ causeway US carrying the 9 part 9 1 / the , of') score far lower than clean wiki docs, so drop wiki-like docs whose bigram-hit fraction is below roughly half the median of the top-scoring docs; also drop docs whose sentence-ending ' . ' is followed by a lowercase word in most cases. (4) Rank surviving docs by classifier score, take top docs until their gpt2 token count (estimate via len(text)/4 or tiktoken on a budgeted basis) reaches about T; if clean in-domain docs fall short of T, just return that shorter list (it will be cycled) provided it has at least ~0.5T tokens, otherwise fill with the next-highest-scoring clean docs. (5) Shuffle the final selection with CURATE_SEED so order is i.i.d.
history.outcome: dev 1.8301 against 1.9636 for the best at the time, KEPT as the new best

history.idea: Make the purity checks cover the whole document instead of just its head, keeping everything else (dedup, ranking, cycle-vs-fill rule, seeded shuffle) unchanged. (a) For every doc that survives dedup and has classifier score >= 0.3, cut 3 extra windows of P chars (middle, three-quarter point, last P chars; skip windows the doc is too short for). Score them with the already-fitted hashing/TF-IDF/LogisticRegression, and set the doc's final score to the minimum over the head and these windows. (b) Compute the target word-bigram hit fraction on up to 4 evenly spaced 300-word windows across the full doc, not only the first 300 words. Drop the doc if any window falls below 0.5x the median hit fraction of the top-scoring docs. (c) Apply the "' . ' followed by a lowercase word" test per window as well, dropping the doc if any window with at least 5 sentence breaks has a lowercase fraction above 0.5. (d) Replace the "same first 200 chars" near-duplicate key with two keys, normalised chars 0-200 and normalised chars 300-500 where the doc is long enough, and drop a doc if either key was seen, so copies with a perturbed header are also caught. Keep runtime bounded by only windowing docs with score >= 0.3.
history.outcome: dev 1.8288 against 1.8301 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Two changes aimed at keeping the training stream purely clean in-domain text; everything else (classifier, damage tests, seeded shuffle) stays the same. (1) Reorder the filters: run the damage tests (line repetition, compressibility, ' . '-then-lowercase, target-bigram hit fraction) on ALL docs first, and only then deduplicate among the undamaged survivors. Within a duplicate group (same whitespace-normalised full text, or same first 200 normalised chars), keep the copy with the highest classifier score, breaking ties by the higher bigram-hit fraction and then the shorter length, instead of the longest copy. Today the longest copy wins the dedup and, if it is then dropped as damaged, its clean twin is lost too. (2) Change the cycle-vs-fill rule: once the docs with score >= 0.5 are exhausted, stop and return only those (the trainer cycles them) whenever they total at least 0.15T tokens, instead of the current 0.5T; only fill with lower-scoring docs below 0.15T. Also log or assert the estimated in-domain token total so the effect can be read off.
history.outcome: dev 1.8540 against 1.8301 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Clean and re-rank the FILL part of the stream (docs with classifier score < 0.5), leaving the in-domain part (score >= 0.5), dedup, cycle-vs-fill rule and seeded shuffle unchanged. Today the damage tests only apply to score >= 0.5 docs, so fill is picked by a wiki-format char classifier and can include spam, letter-scrambled text and code. Changes: (a) Compute the target word-bigram hit fraction (first 300 words, lowercased) and a target-vocabulary word hit fraction (share of the doc's alphabetic words that appear in the target_sample word set) for ALL deduped docs. (b) Drop fill candidates that are junk: (i) template spam: build document frequencies of word 4-grams over the pool (first 150 words per doc, hashed) and drop docs where more than 30% of their 4-grams occur in >= 15 other docs, plus drop docs with zlib ratio < 0.3; (ii) letter-scrambled text: target-vocab word hit fraction < 0.6; (iii) code/markup: share of chars that are letters or spaces < 0.80, or more than 3% of chars in '{}[]();=<>_#/\\'; (iv) word-shuffled: the existing ' . '-then-lowercase test and bigram hit fraction < 0.4x the median of the remaining fill candidates. (c) Rank the surviving fill docs by bigram hit fraction (descending) instead of classifier score, and take them after all in-domain docs until the 1.02T budget is reached. (d) Print the estimated token totals for in-domain docs, clean fill available and fill used, so the split can be read off.
history.outcome: dev 1.8640 against 1.8301 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Keep the selected set exactly as in the current best (same classifier, dedup, damage tests, cycle-vs-fill rule) and change only the ORDER and the budget precision, turning the stream into a curriculum that ends on pure in-domain text. (1) After selection, split the selected docs into fill (classifier score < 0.5) and in-domain (score >= 0.5). (2) Count gpt2 tokens exactly with tiktoken (encode_ordinary_batch, disallowed specials off) for the selected docs instead of the chars/token estimate. (3) Trim the selection to a total of T to 1.003T tokens by dropping the LOWEST-scoring fill docs first, never in-domain docs, so that the trainer's cut-off at T does not remove in-domain text from the end. (4) Emit the order as: all fill docs first (seeded shuffle among themselves), then all in-domain docs (seeded shuffle among themselves). If there is no fill (in-domain alone reaches T, or the cycle branch was taken), fall back to the current plain seeded shuffle. (5) Print the exact token totals of in-domain and fill so the split is visible.
history.outcome: dev 1.8349 against 1.8301 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Keep the classifier, dedup, damage tests and fill ranking exactly as in the current best, and change only how the T budget is split: upweight the clean in-domain docs by repeating them once. After the filters, let IN be the surviving docs with score >= 0.5 and D their estimated token total (same chars/token estimate). (a) If D >= 1.02T, behave as now. (b) If 2D <= 1.02T, put every IN doc in the selection twice, then fill the remaining budget (1.02T - 2D) with the next-highest-scoring surviving docs with score < 0.5, as the current fill does. (c) If D < 1.02T < 2D, include all IN docs once, then add second copies of IN docs in descending score order until the budget is reached, with no fill. Remove the old 'stop at 0.5T and cycle' branch, since these rules replace it. Finally do one seeded shuffle over the whole list, so the two copies of a doc land at independent random positions. Print D, the fill tokens used and the number of repeated docs so the split can be read off.
history.outcome: dev 1.8607 against 1.8301 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Keep the in-domain part (score >= 0.5 after dedup and damage tests), the budget, the fill-vs-cycle rule and the final seeded shuffle exactly as in the current best. Change only how the fill docs (score < 0.5 survivors) are ranked, using a self-trained, format-independent second classifier. (1) Positives: target_sample chunks plus all surviving pool docs with char-classifier score >= 0.9, capped at 4000 by seeded sample. Negatives: a seeded sample of up to 4000 surviving docs with score < 0.05. (2) Features: word-level HashingVectorizer (analyzer='word', lowercase=True, ngram_range=(1,2), 2**18 features, alternate_sign=False) with sublinear TF-IDF on the first 3000 chars. The default token pattern ignores punctuation and '=' headers, so the model learns encyclopedic topic and register rather than WikiText formatting. Fit LogisticRegression(C=1, class_weight='balanced'). (3) Score every fill candidate with this word model. Convert both the original char score and the word score to rank percentiles among the fill candidates, and order the fill by the mean of the two percentiles, descending. Take fill in that order after all in-domain docs until the 1.02T budget. Do not add any new hard drop filters to the fill. If the second fit fails or there are fewer than 200 positives, fall back to the current ordering.
history.outcome: dev 1.8318 against 1.8301 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea:
Add a typo-robust fuzzy near-duplicate pass based on word shingles. Keep the classifier, damage tests, budget, fill ranking, cycle-vs-fill rule and seeded shuffle unchanged.

Run it after the existing exact/first-200-chars dedup and the damage tests:

1. For every surviving doc, lowercase and split it into words, form all word 5-grams over the whole doc, and hash each with zlib.crc32. Keep as the doc's sketch only the shingles whose hash % 8 == 0.

2. Build a pool vocabulary: words that occur in at least 5 pool docs, or anywhere in target_sample. For each doc compute its OOV rate, the share of its alphabetic words (first 2000 words) not in that vocabulary. This is a proxy for character-level typo damage, as in 'Ottawa Senatos' or 'ounded'.

3. Process the surviving docs in order of OOV rate rounded to 0.01 ascending, then length descending, so cleaner and fuller copies come first. Maintain a global set of sketch hashes already seen. For a doc with at least 6 sketch shingles, if more than 50% of them are already in the set, drop it as a near-duplicate, typo-perturbed copy or contained excerpt of a kept doc. Otherwise keep it and add its sketch to the set.

4. Continue with the current ranking and fill, so the freed budget goes to the next-best docs.

Print how many docs and estimated tokens the fuzzy pass removed, split by score >= 0.5 and < 0.5.
history.outcome: dev 1.8336 against 1.8301 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea:
Re-admit the word-shuffled in-domain docs as priority fill, replacing the lowest-scoring generic web fill. Keep the classifier, dedup, clean in-domain set, 1.02T budget and final seeded shuffle unchanged.

1. During the damage tests, do not simply discard docs that fail ONLY the word-order tests (the ' . '-then-lowercase test, or the target-bigram hit fraction below 0.5x median) and that have classifier score >= 0.5. Put them in a separate list SHUF. They must still pass dedup, line repetition and compressibility. Docs failing line repetition or compressibility stay dropped.

2. Because the lowercase test currently runs before the bigram test, compute both for every doc so that SHUF membership is well defined. A doc with score < 0.5 that fails the lowercase test stays dropped as now.

3. Build the stream as:
   - all clean in-domain docs (score >= 0.5, undamaged), as now;
   - then SHUF docs in descending classifier score, up to a cap of 0.30T estimated tokens;
   - then the usual fill (score < 0.5 survivors, by descending classifier score) until 1.02T is reached.

4. Cycle rule: if clean in-domain plus admitted SHUF reaches 1.02T, stop there. Remove the 'stop at 0.5T and cycle' early exit for this run, so the budget is always filled in the order above.

5. Do one seeded shuffle over the whole selection.

6. Print the estimated token totals for clean in-domain, SHUF available, SHUF used and generic fill used.
history.outcome: dev 1.9542 against 1.8301 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea:
Remove word-shuffled documents from the FILL part (classifier score < 0.5) with two format-independent word-order tests. Today the word-order tests only catch WikiText-formatted docs (spaced ' . ', or score >= 0.5), so shuffled ordinary web text can enter the fill unchecked. Keep the classifier, dedup, in-domain set, fill ranking by classifier score, 1.02T budget, cycle-vs-fill rule and seeded shuffle unchanged. Do not add any spam, code or vocabulary filters, and do not re-rank the fill.

1. Attached-punctuation test, for every deduped doc with score < 0.5: in the first 20000 chars, find matches of the regex r"[a-z]{2,}[.!?] ([A-Za-z])" (a word ending a sentence, then the first letter of the next word). If there are at least 5 matches and more than 50% of the following letters are lowercase, drop the doc as shuffled.

2. Generic bigram test:
   - Build a reference set of lowercased word bigrams from target_sample plus the first 3000 words of every clean surviving in-domain doc (score >= 0.5, passed all current tests).
   - For every fill candidate with at least 20 words, compute the fraction of its bigrams (first 300 words) that are in the reference set.
   - Let m be the median of that fraction over the 3000 highest-scoring fill candidates. Drop fill candidates whose fraction is below 0.45*m.

3. Take the fill from the remaining candidates in descending classifier score, as now.

4. Print the docs and estimated tokens dropped by each test, and the estimated tokens of in-domain, fill available and fill used, so a fill shortage is visible.
history.outcome: dev 1.8373 against 1.8301 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea:
Make the token budget exact, so the trainer's cut-off at T never removes in-domain text, and keep the plain seeded shuffle. Classifier, dedup, damage tests, fill ranking and the cycle-vs-fill rule stay as in the current best. This is not the curriculum of experiment 5: fill and in-domain docs are still mixed by one global shuffle.

1. Build the ranked selection as now, but over-select to about 1.15T estimated tokens so there is slack. Take all surviving docs with score >= 0.5, then fill by descending classifier score.

2. Count gpt2 tokens exactly for every selected doc with tiktoken (enc.encode_ordinary_batch over the full text, 8 threads), not the chars/token estimate. The estimate is calibrated on the first 5000 chars of top-ranked wiki docs and is likely wrong for web, code or markup fill.

3. Walk the ranked list (in-domain first, then fill by descending score) and accumulate exact tokens. Stop at the first doc where the total reaches T, and include that doc. The final list then totals between T and T plus one doc. The lowest-scoring fill is what gets left out, never an in-domain doc.

4. If the docs with score >= 0.5 alone exceed T, trim the lowest-scoring of them the same way. If all survivors total less than T, return them all.

5. Apply the existing 'stop at 0.5T and cycle' rule with exact counts.

6. Do one seeded shuffle of the final list, as now.

7. Print the exact in-domain tokens, fill tokens used, and the old estimated total against the exact total, so the size of the estimation error is visible.
history.outcome: dev 1.8352 against 1.8301 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea:
Sharpen the word-order (shuffle) test for in-domain docs with a self-trained reference and a data-driven threshold. Keep the classifier, dedup, line-repetition and compressibility tests, fill ranking, 1.02T budget, cycle-vs-fill rule and seeded shuffle unchanged.

1. Run the current pipeline up to the damage tests. Call the surviving docs with score >= 0.5 the set CLEAN0.

2. Build a bigger reference set of lowercased word bigrams: those from target_sample plus those from the first 2000 words of every CLEAN0 doc whose current bigram hit fraction is at or above the median of CLEAN0 (the confidently unshuffled ones).

3. For every deduped doc with score >= 0.5, including those the old test would drop, recompute the hit fraction against this reference. Use up to 1500 words taken as 5 evenly spaced 300-word windows across the whole doc, pooled into one fraction. Exclude a doc's own bigrams when it contributed to the reference: use bigram document counts and require count >= 2 for contributors, count >= 1 for the rest.

4. Choose the drop threshold from the data rather than the fixed 0.5 x median. Take the hit fractions of all score >= 0.5 docs and find the Otsu threshold (two-class variance-maximising split over a 100-bin histogram). Clamp it to [0.45, 0.85] x the median of the upper class. Drop score >= 0.5 docs below it. Keep the ' . '-then-lowercase test as it is.

5. Do not re-admit the dropped docs as fill. The freed budget goes to the next-best docs by classifier score, as now.

6. Print the threshold, the upper-class median, and the docs and estimated tokens dropped by the old rule against the new rule.
history.outcome: dev 1.8364 against 1.8301 for the best at the time, rejected
